body:
I can confirm that cherry-picking the mentioned pr and trying to compile with `scu_build=yes` in MSVC 14.3 results in the error (i cherry-picked before the change in the pr that replace the `print_verbose` for `WARN_VERBOSE`)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/784c5a90-6d12-444c-a35d-05834addb85f)

The problem is likely due to this, in `variant_utility.cpp` and `variant_utility.h`:
```
#undef print_verbose
```
This means anything that tries to use `print_verbose` after these files will fail (unless it is defined after this point).

We can't do much about the header, but for the cpp, we can add it as an exception from the scu build so it gets compiled on its own and doesn't affect any other files.

It likely wasn't due to your PR, but your PR may have inadvertently changed the grouping of which files were compiled together, which exposed this bug.

I'll see if it can be fixed with a simple exception rule.

### UPDATE
The gravy thickens:
```
    process_folder(["core/variant"], ["variant_utility"])
```
It is already added as an exception in the SCU build, so the problem may be the header, and inclusion order. This may be a gotcha of the header (and if so could theoretically also occur in non-scu build). I'll see if there is a sensible fix.

I *think* that `VariantUtility` is providing it's own version of `print_verbose` (instead of the define) so the function can be bound and used by gdscript using the same name.

The problem the `#undef` causes is that any file that includes `variant_utility.h` can no longer use `print_verbose` from c++ _unless_ it includes `core/string/print_string.h` _after_ variant utility. Unfortunately the `clangformat` step re-orders includes, so could inadvertently cause this problem. 🤔 

Yes I confirmed the hypothesis.
Adding:
```
#ifndef print_verbose
#define print_verbose(m_text)             \
{                                     \
			if (is_print_verbose_enabled()) { \
				print_line(m_text);           \
	}                                 \
}
#endif
```
Into `remote_debugger_peer.cpp` solves the problem (although isn't a good proper fix).

Essentially this happens:
* `print_string.h` is included (defining print_verbose)
* Someone includes `variant_utility.h` (undefining it)
* At this stage reincluding `print_string.h` doesn't work as the include guards prevent it running a second time, and `print_verbose` remains undefined.
